Poss-SLPC sro Unveils Next-Generation Steel Alloy for Automotive Sector

Bratislava – Slovak steel producer Poss-SLPC sro announced the launch of a new high-strength steel alloy designed to meet the evolving demands of the automotive industry. The product, branded as AutoFormX, was unveiled at a press conference on Wednesday at the company’s production facility in Košice.

AutoFormX is the result of a three-year R&D initiative involving metallurgists, engineers, and automotive specialists from Slovakia and neighboring countries. According to company officials, the new alloy offers a combination of reduced weight and enhanced durability, aiming to support manufacturers in producing lighter, more fuel-efficient vehicles without compromising safety standards.

“AutoFormX represents a significant step forward in our commitment to delivering advanced materials tailored to the needs of European carmakers,” said Martina Hlaváčová, CEO of Poss-SLPC sro. “The alloy’s unique microstructure allows for a 15% reduction in vehicle component weight while maintaining, and in some cases exceeding, current strength requirements.”

The Slovak Automotive Industry Association welcomed the announcement, noting that the domestic automotive sector, which accounts for 13% of Slovakia’s GDP, is under increasing pressure to innovate. “New materials such as AutoFormX are vital for local manufacturers to stay competitive as EU emissions regulations become more stringent,” said association spokesperson Tomáš Gregor.

Market analysts estimate that initial production runs of AutoFormX will achieve an annual output of 40,000 metric tons, with Poss-SLPC sro already in talks with several regional parts suppliers. “We expect this alloy to be particularly attractive to Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers looking to streamline their supply chains within Central Europe,” noted Jana Mikulová, a steel industry analyst at Bratislava-based consultancy MetMark Advisors.

Poss-SLPC sro employs over 1,200 people and has a longstanding presence in the eastern Slovak region, where steel production forms a key part of the local economy. The company has invested more than €18 million in upgrading its facilities over the past five years to accommodate advanced alloy production.

Company officials stated that AutoFormX will be available to customers beginning in September, with additional capacity expansions planned if demand meets expectations. “We are confident that this launch will reinforce Slovakia’s position as a hub for high-value steel innovation,” Hlaváčová added.
